At any given moment in my daily life, I have at least five devices needing daily charging and half a dozen more screaming for updates. I used to not mind this so much, but it seems to be that the amount of attention these devices that are supposed to make my life simpler now require is increasing exponentially. For example, I update my smartphone apps to get everything up to date and less than an hour later, I get a message that I have six apps updates available. I go to print something, but my printer says it needs to update before I can print. I shutdown my laptop and ready it for transport, but nope...it's installing updates now and I have to wait for it to finish. Then my tablet alerts me it needs a charge. I plug it in and now my phone is alerting me for charge too. I go to play a game, and oh look, I have to install a major update before I can play. It's like a never ending hell of charging, updating and alerting that won't give me peace. How do you cope with this Voat?
So many devices and gadgets in our lives need daily charging and frequent software updates. Is this something you just accept or do you wish for a simpler world without this?
I don't let it get to me

I've got a low bandwidth cap and I'm definitely not a fan of all the updating. Most systems today are designed without bandwidth in mind. Even when I buy an xbox game on a physical disc there's a good chance it will require a ~10 GB update. It wouldn't be as big a problem if ISP infrastructure kept up with what content creators assume is universal.

Edit: I did make a subverse called /v/DigitalDivide that has some resources for the bandwidth impaired. The problem is that we're swimming against the tide at this point :P even so, there are some limited offline alternatives to online services that are worth checking out.

You can set updates to be automatic, that's usually safe for signed code.

Anyone can have a simpler world by getting rid of their devices... Few do.

I'm using a rolling release on Linux. This means that I decide when to update. Since there is no auto update set up at the moment I need to run a command manually to check for updates. I usually do it once a week. It is actually too bleeding edge for my taste, so I give it one week for the patches to mature, so if there is something wrong in the latest update it will get fixed before I get it.

Linux really has solved the update thing like nobody else. Take this for example Not only it updates everything to the latest and greatest version but once done it will actually take 1.42 MB less space on the HDD! Somebody has removed 1.42 MB of bloat!

How do you feel about outsourcing? If a company can provide it's nation's consumers with a less expensive products by outsourcing jobs is that for the better or worse and why?

I would have to say it is for the worse because allowing companies that seek profits to outsource to different countries may result in lower prices in some cases, these companies can evade wage laws, environmental protections, workplace safety regulation, taxes, and can lead to the disregard of quality rules (which can drastically hurt us the consumers of the products). In other words, outsourcing is for the worse because it allows businesses to cut corners and treat workers worse off while keeping money they saved from cutting corners for whatever they choose to do with it.  

If your interested, this economic comic goes over topics such as outsourcing and the TPP. You might find it interesting.

Outsourcing, to me anyway, has always been just another race to the bottom. Companies seek to pay the least to make their products while charging the most they can get away with. The idea that profit is the most important aspect of a business has taken over all other reasons to be in business. It seems like most corporations have zero interest in what they are making or doing for people or the world and only care about making record profits. There was a time, not that long ago really, that businesses invested in people and actually cared about them. The 80s opened the door to extreme greed and reducing workers to numbers. Outsourcing took root after the people in a business became nothing more than resources and needed to be obtained as cheaply as any other material resource to boost profits. I've worked for Fortune 500 companies that would not bat an eye to lose $20 million due to a failed project. These same companies would writhe in pain if someone even brought up the idea of spending a few thousand dollars to give some a raise or improve the workers' environment. In one breath they will tell you how they need to cut jobs and move overseas to reduce costs while simultaneously boasting of the last quarter's phenomenal results.

Providing the nation with less expensive products means nothing when the jobless rate skyrockets due to outsourcing. If consumers can't afford to buy the latest gadget, why bother trying to sell it to them? You can't undermine the base of the economy and expect to reap profits forever. Outsourcing is not a good thing to me. It only serves the elite and wealthy.

Well said, I came here to say pretty much this. I make a point of buying Canadian/American goods whenever I can even if they cost a bit more, because I know someone didn't work in a sweatshop to make it.

As someone who does IT work for a BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) I can tell you that outsourcing is bullshit. My company provides two sorts of outsourcing, the first is when a company wants to have their shit done cheaper by Americans. The second is having it done by someone in another country. While the first type of outsourcing causes me no small amount of headaches, the second is a whole new sort of hell to deal with. We have an office in the Philippines and while they are hard working they fuck up at an astonishing rate, however the higher ups don't care as we can get something like 4 agents in the Philippines for the price of a US agent. Also many big companies are now requiring the firms they outsource things like customer service, collections and what not to have an international office otherwise they won't play ball.
